LESSON: CHEMICAL BONDING

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: CHEMISTRY
Strand: Inorganic chemistry
Topic 1.4: Chemical Bonding
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 24

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Chemical Bonding, part of Inorganic chemistry in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10 CHEMISTRY.

Key inquiry question: How do chemical bonds influence the properties of substances?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. illustrate bond types in elements, molecules and compounds,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Chemical Bonding in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. investigate the relationship between bond types and physical properties of elements, molecules and compounds,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Chemical Bonding in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. relate bond types and resultant structures to the uses of elements, molecules and compounds,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Chemical Bonding in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. illustrate bond types in elements, molecules and compounds,

   Chemical Bonding helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. investigate the relationship between bond types and physical properties of elements, molecules and compounds,

   Chemical Bonding helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. relate bond types and resultant structures to the uses of elements, molecules and compounds,

   Chemical Bonding helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Chemical Bonding together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Learning to learn: as the learner learns independently while drawing dot and cross diagrams to illustrate bonding

in elements and compounds.

● Digital literacy: as the learner uses digital technology to effectively accomplish own task while watching

animations, simulations, and videos on chemical bonding.

18

● Creativity and Imagination: as the learner experiments with material to develop models to illustrate bonding in

selected elements/compounds using locally available materials.

● Critical Thinking and Problem Solving: as the learner interprets and infer with peers the relationship between bond

types and resulting structures.

Values:
Love: as the learner shows care by avoiding to hurt others as they carry out activities to investigate the physical

properties of different structures.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

● Socio-Economic and Environmental issues (Environment conservation): as the learner uses locally available

materials to make models.

● Life skills (creative thinking): as the learner models bonding in selected elements/compounds e.g., SiO2, NaCl,

graphite and diamond.

● Socio-Economic and Environmental issues (social cohesion): as the learner discusses with peers different types of

chemical bonds.

Suggested learning resources:

Conventional and adapted laboratory resources(beakers, voltmeters and test tubes), adapted digital resources(text to

speech software, expanded keyboards with key guards and sticky keys), positioning devices (chest and neck

braces),adapted writing resources(padded pens/pencils with enhanced grip and book holders),stationary(manilla

papers, marker pens),improvised resources from the environment, related service providers(occupational

therapist),print and non-print media(simulations/videos on chemical bonding and resultant structures)

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

Main points to remember:

1. illustrate bond types in elements, molecules and compounds,
2. investigate the relationship between bond types and physical properties of elements, molecules and compounds,
3. relate bond types and resultant structures to the uses of elements, molecules and compounds,

Remember the key question: How do chemical bonds influence the properties of substances?
